title: St. Agatha’s Tower
visualBrief: Malta’s red watchtower, reconstructed with its four unequal projecting corner turrets, splayed base, rounded cordons, flat gun terrace, fishtail merlons, recessed loopholes, rear windows and elevated arched entrance reached by a limestone stair and timber bridge. Two restored roof cannons, drains and mast fittings complete the exterior.

nativeAxes.front: Native +Z faces the mapped southeast entrance, +X is east-northeast along the entrance facade
nativeAxes.origin: Center of the mapped tower footprint, Y=0 at the foot of its scarped base

scaleBasis: The national inventory and custodian describe the square bastioned plan, scarped walls, fishtail battlements and four corner turrets. The custodian records a two-foot roof parapet and roughly3 m turret rise. The source footprint preserves the roughly18 by18.6 m mapped exterior; custodian front/back and rooftop photos establish the 9.4 m reconstructed gun-platform level and 12.8 m battlement tip. Those overall heights are proportional estimates, not published survey dimensions. Current fixed wooden bridge, shallow-arched portal, stone stair, loop/slit pattern and restored cannon carriages follow the custodian’s detailed exterior images.

geographicProposal.evidence: Mapped Red Tower way91447984 carries ref:nicpmi00033, matching the national inventory for Saint Agatha’s Tower and the custodian name/website. Entrance node3898282959 is on the southeast-facing wall and establishes signed native+Z. +X follows the mapped entrance facade toward east-northeast. The projected outline preserves the four slightly unequal corner turrets; scarped foundation and roof elevations are reconstructed from custodian photographs, not claimed surveyed.
geographicProposal.limitations: Terrain contact is at the tower foundation. Stair flight follows the photographed entrance axis and reconstructed rise; hillside retaining walls, the separate star-shaped entrenchment and terrain steps remain map/terrain features.
geographicProposal.notes: Mapped Red Tower way 91447984 and entrance node 3898282959 fix orientation. The modeled stone flight meets the sampled site path and uses a short timber bridge consistent with the custodian’s photograph. PMTiles bridge 35184758581593 represents this approach and is replaced when the model is present. The modeled bridge span uses visual proportions and the surrounding mapped paths remain visible.
geographicProposal.groundContactBasis: The tower center at Y=0 uses the standard Terrarium field. The base extends 0.65 m below that datum and the stair toe fits the draped path.

terrainReference.basis: The native sample at the model footprint center locates the tower and entry stair.

geometrySource: Original deterministic geometry informed by cited dimensions, measured plans and photographs. No downloaded mesh or photographic texture is embedded.
sourceLicense: Original geometry under repository license. Map-derived outline information is attributed to OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0. Reference publications retain their own rights.
materialMethod: Shared material graphs with metric repeat UV0 and original vertex tints; GLB PBR fallback remains self-contained. No per-model texture duplication.
limitations: Main elevation levels, stone step count and small fittings are proportional reconstructions from custodian photographs. The two-foot parapet, approximately3 m turret rise and mapped outline constrain scale; no unpublished surveyed heights are claimed.

The red lime-plaster weathering is an original continuous tint pattern. Inscription plaques preserve location and line structure; historic lettering and heraldic detail are not invented. Cannon forms represent the two restored roof pieces; casting inscriptions and daily flags are omitted.

The surrounding eighteenth-century dry-stone entrenchment, modern adjacent mast, interiors and movable visitor displays are outside this tower exterior asset. Sloping site terrain and the base of the entrance stair depend on the host’s terrain resolution.
reviewStatus: medium-fi; current hash-bound visual acceptance recorded in qa.json

appearance.identity: Red plaster tower on a splayed base, four turret crowns with fishtail merlons, recessed elevated entry and independent timber bridge at the stone stairs.
appearance.master: Original detailed facade, roof fittings and stair geometry with a recessed foundation extension and fitted lowest risers.
appearance.exclusions: The surrounding entrenchment, adjoining mast, interiors and movable exhibits remain separate. The fitted grades describe the ordinary host terrain.
appearance.browser: Authored skyline and district tiers preserve the four turret silhouettes and the separate timber bridge over its open gap. Street and close-up keep the original rail, tread and roof details.
